run_identity.label: Week 6K dq transient model checks
run_identity.note: compares the dq solution with equivalent-circuit theory and with itself; NOT validation against a real machine

balances.ripple_waveform: equilibrium load + 1 Hz, 1 N*m sine (2.8% of T_avg)
balances.note: the step residual is the quasi-static reduction gap (dq-frame core-loss bookkeeping term), NOT RK4 truncation; reported as a finding.

unbalance.committed_plan_note: the committed (6) value 3.6440 N*m at s=0.04, a_u=0.02 is NOT reproduced by this model (this run: 1.2920 N*m); it is reported, not chased.

approximations: 1. Lumped dq model; no spatial harmonics, no saturation, no skin effect.

2. Core loss is the flux/frequency-dependent Steinmetz+eddy form (6L, amendment 10): P_core = P_core_nom (lam/lam_nom)^2 [(1-c)(f/f_nom) + c (f/f_nom)^2], applied as a frequency-dependent effective shunt R_c_eff(f) = R_c (f/f_nom)^2 / B(f) in the magnetizing branch of both axes. Synthetic P_core_nom = 151.14 W per phase, alpha = 2, eddy fraction c = 0.5. Reduces to the fixed R_c shunt at f = f_nom.

3. Quasi-static core-loss branch: i_c is driven by the rotational EMF j*omega_e*lambda_m; the branch's own fast transient (pole ~1.86e5 rad/s, measured from the 6-state linearisation) is not integrated, which keeps the committed 4-state step gate. The reduction is exact at electrical steady state and reproduces the committed eigenvalue table.
4. Constant parameters (no temperature feedback in 6K); winding resistance is the cold committed value.
5. Rigid single inertia, viscous + Coulomb friction; no shaft compliance or gear dynamics.
6. Torque from the rotor current and magnetizing flux (the core-loss current makes no torque); see the module docstring.

first_catchers.mutation: no sub-stepping (one RK4 step per output sample)

mutation_check.note: all six mutants were caught; M-6K-4 initially survived because the step gate was checked against a module constant instead of the step simulate() actually uses (fixed, then caught by test 11).

findings.title: committed 7-state explicit shunt-R_c model is stiff
findings.detail: The committed (c) model carries lambda_md, lambda_mq as states with i_c = v_m/R_c; that branch has a pole ~1.86e5 rad/s (6-state linearisation), so the committed N_sub=8 step (80 kHz, dt=1.25e-5 s) violates the committed step gate by ~460x. Resolution: quasi-static 4-state reduction (i_c driven by the rotational EMF), which reproduces the committed 4-state eigenvalue table and the shunt steady state exactly.

findings.title: committed derived torque formula overstates torque with core loss
findings.detail: The committed (c) torque T_e = (3/2)p(lambda_md i_qs - lambda_mq i_ds) is the no-core-loss identity. With the R_c shunt it overstates torque (37.35 vs 36.10 N*m at s=0.04, +3.5%) and FAILS the committed test 1 (4.0% > 1.7e-2). Implemented torque uses the rotor current: T_e = (3/2)p(lambda_mq i_dr - lambda_md i_qr).

findings.title: committed eigenvalue table is the R_c-removed 4-state matrix
findings.detail: The committed (1) table matches the R_c-removed 4-state matrix to 4 decimals. The implemented shunt model shifts the running eigenvalues by ~0.1% (s=0.04 |lambda|max 307.765 vs 307.684); the step gate uses the implemented value |lambda|max=307.765 rad/s.

findings.title: committed-test-1 convention gap is slip-dependent, not 1.68%
findings.detail: The committed tol_1=1.7e-2 was set from the fixed-V^2/R_c core-loss offset (1.68% of T_max), but the two models share a core loss, so the actual gap is ~0.5-0.8% over the operating range and grows as T -> 0: measured 8.7e-2 at s=0.001 and 3.1e-2 at s=1.0. Test 1 therefore gates over the committed operating range s in [0.02, 0.25]; the full curve is recorded.

findings.title: the linearisation duplicated the nonlinear flux RHS
findings.detail: electrical_matrix() originally carried its own copy of the four flux equations, so a sign error in derivatives() was invisible to every steady-state test (found by mutant M-6K-3). The RHS is now single-sourced in _electrical_rhs() and the mutant is caught by test 1.

findings.title: dq-frame core-loss bookkeeping term for moving operating points
findings.detail: The exact power identity in the rotating frame carries an extra term P_cross = (3*omega_e/R_c)*(lambda_md dlambda_mq/dt - lambda_mq dlambda_md/dt) that vanishes at steady state. It makes the integral energy residual over a 1 s full-load step ~1.6e-6 (vs 1e-6 tolerance); a small-signal 1 Hz ripple gives ~1e-10. Tests 4/5 use the ripple and the step residual is reported.

core_loss_form.implementation: frequency-dependent effective shunt R_c_eff(f) = R_c (f/f_nom)^2 / B(f)

sensitivity.definition: torque_rel / energy_rel are the relative change vs baseline of the 1 s average torque and total input energy at the slip-0.04 mechanical equilibrium; energy_core_J is the integrated core-loss energy.
sensitivity.note: the core loss enters the torque only through lambda_m (g << K), so the torque effect is small; the energy effect is the direct core-loss change. Both are measured, not derived. At f_nom with c=0.5 the hysteresis and eddy contributions are equal, so kh+50 == ke+50 and kh-50 == ke-50: the f_nom sensitivity cannot distinguish k_h from k_e (that distinction needs f != f_nom).

approximations: 1. Lumped dq model; no spatial harmonics, no saturation, no skin effect.

2. Synthetic P_core_nom = 151.14 W per phase, alpha = 2, eddy fraction c = 0.5. Reduces to the fixed R_c shunt at f = f_nom.

3. Quasi-static core-loss branch: i_c is driven by the rotational EMF j*omega_e*lambda_m; the branch's own fast transient (pole ~1.86e5 rad/s, measured from the 6-state linearisation) is not integrated, which keeps the committed 4-state step gate. The reduction is exact at electrical steady state and reproduces the committed eigenvalue table.

findings.title: flux/frequency-dependent core loss applied (amendment 10)
findings.detail: The fixed shunt R_c is replaced by the approved form P_core = P_core_nom (lam/lam_nom)^2 [(1-c)(f/f_nom) + c (f/f_nom)^2] (alpha=2, c=0.5), applied as a frequency-dependent effective shunt R_c_eff(f) = R_c (f/f_nom)^2/B(f). With alpha=2 the flux dependence is already carried by the shunt; the new physics is B(f). At f=f_nom the model reduces to the 6K fixed shunt (R_c_eff = R_c).

findings.title: the dq model now runs at variable supply frequency
findings.detail: f_Hz is threaded through supply/aux/derivatives/simulate/steady_state/electrical_matrix so the frequency-dependent core loss is exercised; this is what the 6M VSD pump case needs. The inductances stay at the committed values (reactances scale with f automatically).
